Metrics — query / dry-run

USAGE
  openbkn bkn metric [options] [command]

READ
  list [options] <kn-id>                List metrics
  get [options] <kn-id> <metric-id>     Get a metric → {entries}, since the route takes a list of ids

RUN
  query [options] <kn-id> <metric-id>   Query a metric's data (--body / --body-file JSON)
  dry-run [options] <kn-id>             Dry-run a metric definition (--body / --body-file JSON)
  validate [options] <kn-id>            Validate a metric definition (--body / --body-file)

WRITE
  create [options] <kn-id>              Create metrics (--body / --body-file) → body is {entries:[…]}
  update [options] <kn-id> <metric-id>  Update a metric (--body / --body-file)
  delete [options] <kn-id> <metric-id>  Delete a metric

COMMANDS
  help [command]                        display help for command

FLAGS
  -h, --help  display help for command

Knowledge networks: schema, metrics, search, import/export

USAGE
  openbkn bkn [options] [command]

GROUPS
  object-type                                 object-type list/get/...
  relation-type                               relation-type list/get/...
  action-type                                 action-type list/get/...
  action-log                                  Action logs — list/get/cancel; list pages with --search-after
  metric                                      Metrics — query / dry-run
  concept-group                               Concept groups — list/get
  action-schedule                             Action schedules — list/get
  capability                                  Skills, tool box tools and MCP tools bound to a network — list/attach/detach

READ
  list [options]                              List knowledge networks
  get [options] <kn-id>                       Get a knowledge network (use --stats or --export)
  search [options] <kn-id> <query>            Recall instances from a plain sentence — no object type or field names needed → {nodes, object_types}
  stats <kn-id>                               Get knowledge-network statistics (alias for get --stats)
  export <kn-id>                              Export a knowledge network (alias for get --export)
  subgraph [options] <kn-id>                  Query a subgraph (--body / --body-file JSON)
  action-execution <kn-id> <execution-id>     Get action execution status
  pull [options] <kn-id> [directory]          Download a knowledge network as a BKN tar and extract it locally
  relation-type-paths [options] <kn-id>       Query relation-type paths between object types (--body / --body-file JSON)
  cypher [options] <kn-id>                    Answer a read-only Cypher query over the network's model, outside any Trace session
  resources [options]                         List BKN-backend resources (knowledge networks) → {entries, total_count}
  validate <directory>                        Validate a local BKN directory's structure (offline)

WRITE
  create [options] <name>                     Create an (empty) knowledge network
  update [options] <kn-id>                    Update a knowledge network (--body / --body-file)
  delete [options] <kn-id>                    Delete a knowledge network
  push [options] <directory>                  Pack a BKN directory into a tar and import it as a knowledge network
  create-from-catalog [options] <catalog-id>  Build a knowledge network from a Vega catalog's tables

COMMANDS
  help [command]                              display help for command

WHERE IDS COME FROM
  `list` gives kn ids; `object-type list <kn-id>` and `search <kn-id> "<q>"` give the rest.

SEARCH VS THE MCP SIDE
  `search` recalls instance rows from one sentence and ships the object-type definitions
  needed to read them — start here when you do not know the schema yet. It only reaches
  properties indexed for match/knn, so an unindexed object type yields nothing, and no hits
  comes back as empty nodes with a message rather than an error. For schema alone use
  `openbkn context search-schema`; for a structured filter use `object-type query`.

EDITING SCHEMA AS FILES
  pull <kn-id> ./dir  ->  edit  ->  validate ./dir  ->  push ./dir
  `validate` is offline and catches structure errors before the upload.
  network.bkn may declare the skills and tools the network depends on under
  `capabilities:`. push binds them by id, then by name; one this platform cannot
  resolve is skipped, not fatal, and push lists every skip on stderr.

CAPABILITIES
  `capability list <kn-id>` shows what a network has bound — the set Context Loader
  recalls skills and tools from; a network with nothing bound recalls nothing.

REQUEST BODIES
  create/update take a definition; query/execute/dry-run take a query. Both are documented
  at https://openbkn-ai.github.io/bkn-foundry/ — definitions under bkn-backend, reads and
  executions under ontology-query. Each command's --body flag names its own module.

CREATING FROM DATA
  create-from-catalog <catalog-id> --name "<n>" builds a network from a Vega catalog,
  then `openbkn vega resource build <resource-id>` produces the index. There is no
  whole-network build.

FLAGS
  -h, --help  display help for command

Toolboxes: group tools into one publishable box

USAGE
  openbkn toolbox [options] [command]

READ
  list [options]             List toolboxes → {data, total, page, page_size, has_next}; the id is `box_id`
  export [options] <box-id>  Export a toolbox config to a local .adp file

WRITE
  create [options]           Create a toolbox — openapi proxies to a service, function holds platform functions
  publish <box-id>           Publish a toolbox
  unpublish <box-id>         Take a published toolbox down (status=offline)
  delete [options] <box-id>  Delete a toolbox
  import [options] <file>    Import a toolbox config from a local .adp file

COMMANDS
  help [command]             display help for command

TWO KINDS OF BOX
  --type openapi   its tools proxy to --service-url; they come from a spec
  --type function  its tools are platform functions, no service URL to give

  ORDER OF WORK
  toolbox create --name "<n>"        an empty box, not yet published
  tool create ./add.py --toolbox     a function tool, or --type openapi for a spec
  tool debug <tool-id>               call it while building, before enable/publish
  tool enable <tool-ids...>          a tool is off until enabled
  toolbox publish <box-id>           execute needs a published box
  tool execute <tool-id>             call an enabled tool in a published box

  Both gates apply to `execute`: the tool must be enabled and the box published —
  an unpublished or offline box answers 400 ToolNotAvailable. `debug` skips both.

  export / import move a whole box between deploys as an .adp file.

FLAGS
  -h, --help  display help for command

Advanced tools in a box: add one from code or a spec, enable it, call it

USAGE
  openbkn tool [options] [command]

READ
  list [options]                     List tools in a toolbox
  get [options] <tool-id>            One tool in full: metadata, parameters, usage rule

RUN
  execute [options] <tool-id>        Invoke an enabled tool in a published toolbox
  debug [options] <tool-id>          Invoke a tool before it is enabled or its toolbox published

WRITE
  enable [options] <tool-ids...>     Enable one or more tools
  disable [options] <tool-ids...>    Disable one or more tools
  create [options] <file>            Create a tool from code (or a spec)
  update [options] <tool-id> <file>  Replace a tool's definition; the id survives and an enabled tool stays enabled
  delete [options] <tool-ids...>     Delete tools from a toolbox
  upload [options] <file>            Add tools from an OpenAPI file — `tool create` is the same endpoint, as JSON

COMMANDS
  help [command]                     display help for command

  -h, --help  display help for command

Skill packages (SKILL.md + files) agents load on demand

USAGE
  openbkn skill [options] [command]

READ
  list [options]                             List skills → {data, total, page, page_size, has_next}; the id to reuse is `skill_id`
  get <skill-id>                             Get a skill by id
  market [options]                           Browse the skill market → {data, total, page, has_next}
  market-get <skill-id>                      Get a market skill by id
  content [options] <skill-id>               Read a skill's SKILL.md content index
  read-file [options] <skill-id> <rel-path>  Read a file inside a skill (progressive)
  files [options] <skill-id> [path]          List a skill's files (one level; --tree for the whole hierarchy)
  names <ids...>                             Resolve skill ids to names (unknown ids are skipped)
  history <skill-id>                         Show a skill's version history

RUN
  execute [options] <skill-id>               Run a skill in the platform sandbox
  download [options] <skill-id> [out-path]   Download a skill archive to a local .zip
  install <skill-id> [directory]             Download a skill archive and extract it locally

WRITE
  delete <skill-id>                          Delete a skill
  set-status <skill-id> <status>             Publish or take down a skill: published | offline
  register [options] <directory>             Zip a local skill directory and register it
  update-metadata [options] <skill-id>       Replace a skill's metadata (--body / --body-file JSON: name, description, category required)
  update-package <skill-id> <directory>      Replace a skill's package from a local directory
  republish [options] <skill-id>             Copy a historical version back into the draft (publishes nothing; see publish-history)
  publish-history [options] <skill-id>       Publish a historical skill version directly

COMMANDS
  help [command]                             display help for command

READING A SKILL
  content <id> gives the SKILL.md index; files <id> [path] walks the package; read-file
  pulls one file. Read progressively — do not download the whole archive to answer a question.

PUBLISHED VS DRAFT
  Read commands return the published version. --draft reads the editing copy instead, which
  is what a Studio user sees. The two differ whenever changes are unpublished.

AUTHORING
  register <dir> zips and registers; update-package replaces the files; update-metadata
  changes only the metadata (a full overwrite: name, description, category required).
  set-status publishes or takes down the current version. republish copies a historical
  version back into the draft and publishes nothing; publish-history publishes one.

FLAGS
  -h, --help  display help for command

openbkn — one CLI for the BKN platform: knowledge networks, the data behind them,
the tools and skills agents run on them, and the traces they leave.

USAGE
  openbkn [options] [command]

SIGN IN & SETTINGS
  auth                             Log in; the token is saved and reused. Start here.
  config                           Remember a platform URL
  appkey                           Issue long-lived `bak_` keys for scripts and services

DATA & KNOWLEDGE
  bkn                              Knowledge networks: schema, metrics, search, import/export
  vega                             Data sources: catalogs, connectors, SQL, index builds
  resource|res                     Tables and views behind a network: find, inspect, sample, enable, disable
  context                          Ask a network questions (the MCP interface agents use)

MODELS
  model                            Large and small models: chat, embeddings, rerank, defaults

TOOLS & SKILLS
  skill                            Skill packages (SKILL.md + files) agents load on demand
  mcp                              Registered MCP Servers: inspect their configuration and discover their tools
  sandbox                          Sandbox functions: run Python on the platform without registering anything
  toolbox                          Toolboxes: group tools into one publishable box
  function                         Function Tools in a toolbox: add one, enable it, and call it
  api                              OpenAPI Tools in a toolbox: add one, enable it, and call it
  tool                             Advanced tools in a box: add one from code or a spec, enable it, call it

TRACING
  trace                            Inspect what an agent actually did, and diagnose bad answers

ADMINISTRATION
  admin                            Orgs, users, roles, license, audit log

RAW API
  call|curl [options] <url>        Call any platform API endpoint directly (auth added)

COMMANDS
  describe [options] [command...]  Print the command tree — paths, sections, flags (--json for the data)
  help [command]                   display help for command

FIRST STEPS
    openbkn auth login https://your-platform -u <user> -p <pass>
    openbkn bkn list                       # knowledge networks you can see
    openbkn bkn --help                     # every group has its own help
    openbkn describe --depth 1             # the whole map as one table; `describe <command>`
                                           # drills in, --json ships the same tree as data

  COMMON TASKS
    Answer a question    bkn search <kn-id> "<q>"  ->  context search-schema  ->
                         context query-object-instance --args '<json>'
    Look at the data     vega catalog list  ->  resource find --name <t>  ->  resource query <id>
    Build from a catalog bkn create-from-catalog <catalog-id> --name "<n>"  ->
                         vega resource build <resource-id>
    Edit as files        bkn pull <kn-id> ./kn  ->  bkn validate ./kn  ->  bkn push ./kn
    Ship an API          toolbox create --name "<n>" --service-url <url>  ->
                         api import ./api.yaml --toolbox <box-id>  ->
                         api enable <tool-id> --toolbox <box-id>  ->  toolbox publish <box-id>
                         ->  api execute <tool-id> --toolbox <box-id>
    Ship some code       sandbox run ./add.py  ->  toolbox create --name "<n>" --type function
                         ->  function create ./add.py --toolbox <box-id> --name add  ->
                         function enable <tool-id> --toolbox <box-id>  ->
                         toolbox publish <box-id>  ->  function execute <tool-id> --toolbox <box-id>
    Debug an answer      trace conversations list  ->  trace diagnose <conversation-id> --llm

  GOOD TO KNOW
    Every command group sorts its subcommands into the same four sections: GROUPS nests one
    level deeper, READ changes nothing, RUN acts without changing configuration (triggers a
    job, spends a model call, rotates a token), WRITE changes platform state — confirm those
    with a person first.
    Add --json to any command for machine-readable output (the default view trims columns,
    --full widens it). Most list commands answer {entries, total_count}; anything else says
    so in its own description. Ids come from list/search output — opaque, never guess one,
    and the key holding one is not always `id` (`skill_id`, `conversation_id`, `ot_id` …).
    Saved logins are selected with --user; access follows the account's platform grants.
    `openbkn call` reaches any endpoint a command does not cover, auth injected. Look the
    path up at https://openbkn-ai.github.io/bkn-foundry/ first — do not guess one.

FLAGS
  -V, --version           output the version number
  --base-url <url>        platform base URL (env: BKN_BASE_URL)
  --token <value>         access token (env: BKN_TOKEN)
  --user <id|name>        use specific user credentials (env: BKN_USER)
  --json                  machine-readable JSON output
  --compact               single-line JSON output
  --full                  human view: show all columns (default trims to the key ones)
  --conversation-id <id>  BKN Trace conversation id (env: BKN_CONVERSATION_ID)
  --interaction-id <id>   BKN Trace interaction id (env: BKN_INTERACTION_ID)
  --new-conversation      ignore the remembered conversation for this command (see `openbkn context conversation`)
  -k, --insecure          skip TLS verification (dev / self-signed only)
  --no-retry              fail at once on a refused/dropped connection or a 429/502/503, instead of retrying 3 times
  --dry-run               print the request this command would send, and send nothing
  --skip-version-check    send the request even if the platform version does not match this SDK (env: BKN_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1)
  -h, --help              display help for command
